module_title: Indian Monsoon and Seasons - Basic Understanding
introduction: India has a 'Tropical Monsoon' type of climate. The word 'Monsoon' is derived from the Arabic word 'Mausim', which literally means the 'seasonal reversal of the direction of winds' over a year.

core_concepts.title: The 4 Main Seasons of India
core_concepts.description: 1. Winter (Mid-Dec to Feb). 2. Summer (March to May). 3. Advancing Monsoon / South-West Monsoon (June to Sept). 4. Retreating Monsoon / North-East Monsoon (Oct to Nov).

core_concepts.title: South-West (SW) Monsoon
core_concepts.description: This brings about 75-80% of India's total rainfall. It enters India in two main branches: The Arabian Sea Branch and the Bay of Bengal Branch.

core_concepts.title: Arabian Sea Branch
core_concepts.description: It is the first to hit the Indian mainland. It strikes the Malabar Coast of Kerala around June 1st, bringing heavy rainfall to the Western Ghats.

core_concepts.title: Bay of Bengal Branch
core_concepts.description: It moves towards Myanmar and Northeast India. Due to the funnel shape of the Garo, Khasi, and Jaintia hills in Meghalaya, it gets trapped and causes extremely heavy rainfall.

important_entities.name: Mawsynram
important_entities.significance: Located in the Khasi Hills of Meghalaya, it receives the highest average annual rainfall in the world (approx. 11,872 mm) primarily from the Bay of Bengal branch.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: In common language, people use 'monsoon' as a synonym for rain. In geography, monsoon strictly means the 'reversal of wind direction'. The rain is just a byproduct of these moisture-laden winds.

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Always remember that the monsoon officially enters the Indian mainland through the state of Kerala (on the Western Ghats).

exam_strategy_tips: The etymology of the word Monsoon (Arabic word 'Mausim') is a very common question in basic GK exams.
If asked about India's climate type, the standard answer is always 'Tropical Monsoon'.
